claims.text: Significant lattice distortions are the primary factor governing the high-temperature structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
High-entropy nanoalloys inherently possess significant lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions create kinetic or energetic barriers to atomic mobility.
The barriers associated with lattice distortion slow atomic diffusion in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Slower atomic diffusion reduces the rate of phase segregation during high-temperature exposure.
Slower atomic diffusion reduces chemical decomposition during high-temperature exposure.
After identical annealing, high-entropy nanoalloys will show less phase separation than lower-complexity control nanoalloys.
After identical annealing, high-entropy nanoalloys will show less chemical segregation than lower-complexity control nanoalloys.
High compositional entropy necessarily produces significant lattice distortions in the proposed samples.
The prediction is intended to apply to high-entropy nanoalloys annealed in an inert atmosphere between 800°C and 1200°C.
Comparable or greater diffusion in the high-entropy samples relative to the lower-entropy controls would falsify the proposed sluggish-diffusion mechanism.
Failure of the high-entropy samples to show reduced phase segregation relative to controls would falsify the proposed stability mechanism.
